extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (issuers), their auditors/assurance providers, corporate counsel, and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and disclosure standards from the SEC final rules governing registrant climate-related disclosures, including GHG emissions (Scope 1 and 2), assurance/attestation, risk management processes, and related financial-statement expenditure disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants required to disclose Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions (subject to phased compliance dates), except that SRCs and EGCs are exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures improve investor understanding of exposure to material climate-related risks, management of that risk, and progress on transition plans. Registrants that only measure some Scope 1/2 emissions should report the information they have. The final rules permit reasonable estimates (see separate criterion) and require contextual disclosures (methodology, boundaries, inputs, assumptions, reporting standard) to aid comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure controls and procedures apply to GHG emissions disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions disclosures, to the extent required, must be subject to registrants' disclosure controls and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjecting these disclosures to disclosure controls and procedures is intended to improve accuracy and reliability of the information provided to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of reasonable estimates for Scope 1 and 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may disclose reasonable estimates for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions provided such estimates are accompanied by disclosure of underlying assumptions and reasons for using estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing reasonable estimates helps registrants provide usable information when precise measurement is not possible; the required accompanying assumptions help investors understand and evaluate the estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contextual disclosures for Scope 1 and 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose methodology, significant inputs, significant assumptions, organizational boundaries, operational boundaries, and reporting standard used with respect to Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These contextual disclosures provide additional context to help investors understand quantitative emissions disclosures, facilitate comparisons across registrants, and distinguish differences (e.g., utilities paid directly vs. via lease) that affect reported emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for SRCs and EGCs from GHG emissions and assurance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller Reporting Companies (SRCs) and Emerging Growth Companies (EGCs) are exempted from the GHG emissions disclosure requirement and, as a consequence, from the attestation/assurance requirements tied to those disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption is intended to limit compliance costs and mitigate potential deterrence of IPOs or deregistration among smaller registrants; it may reduce cross-registrant comparability but is deemed appropriate given burden concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregate constituent gases only when individually material
rubrics_metrics.description: Disaggregation of GHG emissions by constituent gases (e.g., methane) is required only when the individual constituent gas is material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This balances decision-usefulness—some gases have differential effects on business operations or regulatory exposure—with the compliance costs of producing disaggregated data. Example: methane disclosure could be material if the registrant faces methane fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in choice of GHG measurement methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may calculate and disclose GHG emissions according to the methodology that best matches their facts and circumstances (e.g., GHG Protocol, ISO standards), and may round as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility allows use of the latest suitable methodologies and limits costs, but may reduce comparability. The required contextual disclosures (operational boundaries, methodology, inputs) and industry-specific approaches evolving over time are expected to mitigate comparability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased compliance schedule for emissions disclosure and assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Two phased-in compliance periods: one before GHG emissions disclosures are required and another later period before assurance over GHG emissions disclosures is required. Specifically, attestation at the limited assurance level for LAFs and AFs begins in the third fiscal year after the GHG emissions reporting compliance date; reasonable assurance requirement applies to LAFs beginning the seventh fiscal year after the compliance date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phased implementation gives registrants time to develop processes/controls and gives assurance providers time to train staff and enter the market, reducing immediate compliance costs and supporting supply of assurance services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance/attestation requirement for LAFs and AFs
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require Certain Large Accelerated Filers (LAFs) and Accelerated Filers (AFs) to provide an attestation report at the limited assurance level for Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions beginning the specified phased-in year; LAFs must provide reasonable assurance beginning in the seventh fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance provides an independent third-party check on accuracy and completeness of GHG disclosures, helping reduce greenwashing risk and improving investor confidence. AFs are not required to provide reasonable assurance (only LAFs are).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation provider expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG emissions attestation report must be prepared and signed by a GHG emissions attestation provider who is an expert in GHG emissions by virtue of having significant experience in measuring, analyzing, reporting, or attesting to GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expertise requirement intended to enhance assurance quality, consistent with evidence that industry-specialist auditors deliver higher quality audits. Providers must also be independent (see independence criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation provider independence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The attestation provider must be independent with respect to the registrant, and any of its affiliates, for whom it is providing the attestation report, during the attestation and professional engagement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence enhances perceived credibility of assurance, analogous to independence requirements for financial statement auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible attestation standards (including ISO 14064-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attestation report pursuant to the ISO 14064-3 standards will satisfy the final rule's requirements. The rules permit registrants to follow any attestation standards that are publicly available at no cost or widely used for GHG emissions assurance and that are established by a body that has followed due process procedures (including broad public comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This modification addresses commenter concerns about precluding non-accountant providers and evolving assurance standards, providing flexibility while ensuring standards are sufficiently developed and publicly vetted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of attestation provider oversight and whether engagement is inspected
rubrics_metrics.description: LAFs and AFs must disclose, after requesting relevant information from any GHG emissions attestation provider as necessary, whether the attestation provider is subject to any oversight inspection program, and if so, which program(s) and whether the engagement is included within the scope of such oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure gives investors information to assess qualifications of the attestation provider and whether assurance services likely enhanced reliability of GHG disclosures. It acknowledges that the rules do not mandate mandatory oversight/inspection but require disclosure of its existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of attestation provider resignation/dismissal and disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: AFs and LAFs subject to Item 1506(a) must disclose whether any GHG emissions attestation provider previously engaged for the fiscal year covered resigned or was dismissed, and if so, describe any disagreements and whether the registrant authorized the former provider to respond fully to successor inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to enable investors to assess possible effects of such disagreements on reliability of GHG disclosures and to limit registrants' incentive to dismiss unfavorable providers. The information is expected to be readily available and not costly to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary assurance disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registrant not required to include a GHG emissions attestation report must disclose certain information if its GHG emissions disclosure were voluntarily subjected to third-party assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater disclosures about voluntary assurance approaches help investors determine whether assurance has enhanced reliability. The rules also amend Rule 436 to provide that descriptions of voluntary assurance under Item 1506(e) are not considered part of the registration statement for sections 7 and 11 liability purposes, mitigating liability-related disincentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management disclosure: process description
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe any processes they have for identifying, assessing, and managing material climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant with such a process should address, as applicable, how it identifies whether it has incurred or is reasonably likely to incur a material physical or transition risk; how it decides whether to mitigate, accept, or adapt to the particular risk; and how it prioritizes addressing the climate-related risk. Also disclose whether and how those processes have been integrated into the registrant's overall risk management system or processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management disclosure: tailored, flexible approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require a descriptive, facts-and-circumstances-tailored discussion of the registrant's processes rather than a set of prescriptive elements (e.g., not requiring a separate disclosure on how a registrant determines how to mitigate high priority risks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility limits compliance costs and the need to disclose potentially confidential information, but may reduce comparability. Registrants may include additional details (as in the proposal) if relevant to their practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement expenditure disclosures: categories required
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers must disclose: (1) expenditures expensed as incurred and losses resulting from severe weather events and other natural conditions; (2) capitalized costs and charges resulting from severe weather events and other natural conditions; and (3) if carbon offsets or RECs were used as a material component of plans to achieve disclosed targets/goals, the aggregate amount of carbon offsets and RECs expensed, the aggregate amount capitalized, and the aggregate amount of losses on capitalized offsets/RECs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures help investors assess the effects of physical risks on financial position and performance and enable cross-company and over-time comparisons. Disclosures are limited to these categories (not transition activities generally) to improve clarity and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of when costs 'result from' severe weather or other natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A capitalized cost, expenditure expensed, charge, loss, or recovery results from a severe weather event or other natural condition when the event or condition is a 'significant contributing factor' in incurring that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attribution standard narrows scope and addresses commenters' hypotheticals about whether routine actions (e.g., replacing a light bulb) would qualify; it focuses disclosures on impacts materially linked to severe weather/natural conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bright-line thresholds for financial-statement disclosure triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of capitalized costs and charges is required if the aggregate absolute amount is one percent or more of the absolute value of shareholders' equity or deficit, but no disclosure if such amount is less than $500,000 for the fiscal year. Disclosure of expenditures expensed and losses is required if aggregate amount is one percent or more of the absolute value of pretax income, but no disclosure if less than $100,000 for the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds aim to ensure investors receive decision-useful information for registrants meaningfully impacted by severe weather/natural conditions while avoiding immaterial reporting. If triggered, registrants must identify where the amounts are presented in the income statement and balance sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: If thresholds triggered, disclose aggregate amounts and statement line items
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosure thresholds are met, registrants must disclose the aggregate amount of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses resulting from severe weather/natural conditions and identify where those amounts are presented in the income statement and balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including presentation location supports investor ability to assess financial statement impacts and compare across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual disclosures to accompany expenditure disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should disclose contextual information alongside expenditure disclosures, such as descriptions of significant inputs and assumptions used, significant judgments made, and, if applicable, policy decisions made to calculate the specified disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual information helps mitigate comparability concerns arising from differing applications, reduces risk of strategic presentation, and supports investor evaluation; inclusion in audited financial statements subjects these disclosures to ICFR and audit oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowed scope of financial disclosures to severe weather and offsets/RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules limit financial statement disclosures to capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions and to capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and RECs, rather than transition activities generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses commenter concerns about ambiguity in defining transition activities and attribution, while recognizing some issuers may apply the rules differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that GHG attestation report be prepared and signed
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require the GHG emissions attestation report to be prepared and signed by the attestation provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed attestation formalizes the engagement and aligns with practices for assurance over other disclosures.
